How does the system stop people from just fabricating bitcoins? I know people can "mine" it, but how is that different than just adjusting values and turning your one into ten?
The system keeps track of every single (and partial) bitcoin all the way back to where they were first generated. Ensuring that there are no "extra" bitcoins on the network

The short answer is: entropy. To change the ledger you would need to re-compute a chain of cryptographic hashes to arrive at an ultra-low entropy information state. To do this you would have to either be extremely lucky (as in, once in a trillion lifetimes of a trillion universes) or you would need significantly more computing power than is currently used by the bitcoin network to arrive at the aforementioned low-entropy configuration.

Bitcoin is essentially an ingenious way of converting energy to (low entropy) information using a distributed network of computers.
